risks: Minimal physical risk; privacy risk from reading paper notes of older patients, many with dementia.
consent: Consent is impracticable for past patients, many of whom lack capacity or have died; a waiver of consent for secondary use will be requested from the research ethics board.
data: Readers record coded variables only on the form; forms carry a study number; the linkage list stays with the clerical supervisor and is destroyed after analysis.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients with dementia, the oldest patients and those admitted from care homes are least represented in the trial evidence and most affected by long stays; the estimate is reported for patients with dementia, and weekend admissions are examined because they wait longest.
effectiveness: The study informs whether weekend physiotherapy cover is worth proposing; a precise null result would redirect effort to other causes of long stays.
grants: None needed; a positive result would support a proposal to test weekend cover.
partnerships: Therapy services management, the orthogeriatric team, the clerical supervisor, and a carer of a former patient with dementia reviewing the plain-language summary.
rebPath: Review by the hospital research ethics board with a request for a waiver of consent; not yet submitted, so the gate is unknown.
limitations: Residual confounding; notes of variable quality; one unit.
summary: Secondary use of paper notes with a waiver request and equity reporting for patients with dementia.
